text: Always import necessary classes and functions at the beginning of your test files to avoid NameErrors. This includes ensuring that any required fixtures are properly defined and accessible.

When using the Console class, remember to set the 'record' parameter to True in the constructor if you intend to capture output. This is a common pitfall that can lead to assertion errors when exporting console contents.
Always import necessary modules at the beginning of your test files to avoid NameErrors, especially for commonly used libraries like 'io'.
Ensure that your assertions match the expected output format precisely, including any escape sequences or formatting characters, to avoid AssertionErrors.

Always ensure that the test case accurately reflects the bug report by verifying the expected behavior against the correct output. This includes checking the specific conditions under which the bug occurs, especially when dealing with character rendering or encoding.

Follow the project's conventions for naming test functions and structuring tests. Use descriptive names that clearly indicate what is being tested, and ensure that the test is placed in the appropriate test file to maintain clarity and organization.
